subject: Re: Proposal — SLA tiers, escalation coverage, and commitment terms
messages:
From: Elliot Ross <elliot.ross@brightcart.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@brightcart.com
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: SLA coverage & discount ask for pilot -> expansion

Jonas —

Thanks for the demo last week. BrightCart is excited by the latency and cost numbers, and the team wants to lock down SLA and support terms before we move to an annual commit. A few specific asks from procurement and legal: 

- We need a 99.95% uptime guarantee for API endpoints behind the production gateway (multi-region) or a clearly defined credit table.
- For P1 incidents we require a 1-hour response commitment (acknowledge + initial triage), P2 within 4 hours.
- We have an internal budget target; is there room for a volume-based discount if we commit to a 12‑month reserved capacity at ~2M generation tokens / month average?
- Legal requests standard escalation coverage (named contacts, twice-daily status updates until resolved, and an optional on-call retainer).

I've attached a usage profile and the high-level procurement checklist. Can you send a proposed SLA+pricing sheet we can use for procurement review?

—Elliot
Elliot Ross
Head of Platform Operations, BrightCart
elliot.ross@brightcart.com
(415) 555-0182

Attachment stubs: brightcart_usage_profile_anon.xlsx
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Elliot Ross <elliot.ross@brightcart.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2027 12:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA coverage & discount ask for pilot -> expansion

Elliot —

Appreciate the clear asks and the usage profile — useful context. I attached a concise SLA/pricing sheet that maps uptime bands, response windows, and a proposed retainer option. High level: 

- Uptime bands: 99.9% (standard), 99.95% (business), 99.99% (enterprise). Credit scale is linear by minute beyond SLO; we included both region-failover and single-region values.
- Response windows: P1 acknowledge target 30–60m (depends on retainer), P1 initial triage + on-call engagement within 1h, P2 within 4h, P3 within 1 business day.
- Retainer: 8/5 vs 24/7 options; retainer reduces remediation time SLAs and increases credit caps.
- Volume discount: we can support stepped discounts at commit tiers (starts at 10% for 12-month 1.5M tokens/month commit, 18% at 2.5M, with an early-payment credit).

Two quick clarifications that will help us finalize pricing: 
1) Is BrightCart comfortable with a multi-region failover configuration (we recommend it for 99.95%+) or will you remain single-region for the pilot?
2) Do you want on-call escalation routed to your SREs + our on-call, or to Redwood-only during the initial pilot?

I copied Vanessa (commercial lead) and Grace (eng ops) to confirm pricing flex and on-call routing. If we get your answers today we can turn around a redline-ready SOW and DocuSign envelope by Monday.

Attachment: redwood_sla_pricing_v1.pdf

Best,
Jonas Weber
Director, Platform Sales — Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai
From: Elliot Ross <elliot.ross@brightcart.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@brightcart.com, Claudia@claralaw.com
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 08:06:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA coverage & discount ask for pilot -> expansion

Jonas — thanks for the prompt response and the sheet. A few follow-ups from procurement & legal: 

- Pilot will be single-region (us-west) for now; plan to enable multi-region in Q3 if metrics hold. That means the 99.95% band is preferable but we need clear crediting for single-region failure modes.
- For escalation routing: for the pilot, routing to Redwood-only on-call is fine as long as we have named contacts and twice-daily updates during P1; we'll transition to joint SRE routing in expansion.
- On volume discounts: the procurement team asked if you can make a firm 15% at the 2M token commit level (which is between your published steps) instead of the bracketed approach. It's important for our internal forecasting.

Legal (Claudia) added: please include a simple explicit clause about incident postmortems within 5 business days for Sev1s and a security contact for SOC2 evidence requests.

If you can send a version with the single-region credit table + a 15% firm discount at 2M commit, we'll aim to get internal exec sign-off quickly.

—Elliot

Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA coverage & discount ask for pilot -> expansion

Elliot —

Thanks for the clarification. We're prepared to make a commercial concession to keep momentum. Proposed changes in the attached: 

- Single-region credit table for 99.95% (pilot) tightened so that credits apply for infrastructure and software-layer downtime; failover misconfigurations excluded.
- Firm 15% volume discount at a 12-month commit of 2M tokens/month (we'll bake this into the SOW with a true-up clause if usage exceeds +/-20% over the average).
- P1 operational guarantee maintained: 1-hour acknowledge + 1-hour initial triage under the retainer; we'll include named escalation contacts and a twice-daily update cadence for Sev1 until resolved.
- Incident postmortem within 5 business days for Sev1s; SOC2 evidence requests will be routed to our security team via security@redwood.ai (we'll include an SLA for response time on evidence requests).

Next steps: if BrightCart confirms the single-region pilot and signs the attached SOW, we will issue a DocuSign envelope with the agreed pricing table and a short MRP to start the reserved capacity provisioning. Grace will coordinate onboarding cadence and the technical kick-off.

Attachment: docusign_brightcart_sla_v2.pdf

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Commercial — Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai

Vanessa / Jonas —

This looks good and I appreciate the flexibility. BrightCart confirms: single-region pilot, acceptance of the firm 15% at 2M tokens/month with the +/-20% true-up clause, and the postmortem / SOC2 contact terms. Please send DocuSign and procurement will route to finance for final sign-off.

I'll expect the envelope and a short onboarding calendar from Grace. If we can have the contract executed by end of next week, we can target provisioning the reserved capacity in early May.

Thanks,
Elliot
